case_title: Hirabhai Jhaverbhai v. State of Gujarat & Ors.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 324 IPC and sentenced to six months imprisonment and fine of Rs.250/-
neutral_facts: The incident in question occurred on July 23, 1986, involving the accused and the victim. The accused was convicted under Section 324 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and sentenced to six months imprisonment and a fine of Rs.250/- in default of payment, which could result in simple imprisonment for 15 days. The victim and the injured parties were impleaded as respondents and filed an affidavit stating that the disputes between the parties had been settled with the intervention of respectable persons of the society and that they were willing to compound the offence. The Court found that the offence was committed before the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2005 came into force, making the offence compoundable with the permission of the Court. Permission to compound the offence was granted to the original complainant and the injured parties, leading to the acquittal of the accused.
